Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the 30-minute demo this morning — great discussion and appreciate the clarity on your pilot objectives. I wanted to capture the procurement/commercial items we discussed and outline a minimal set of next steps so we can move toward a purchase order: 

Quick recap (from our call):
- Pilot scope: 3 teams, ~50K tokens/month during pilot window.
- Goal: validate throughput & cost per inference for 90-day pilot.
- Security: enterprise controls required (VPC + audit logs).

Procurement / commercial questions we flagged:
1) Preferred payment method (PO vs corporate card) and internal threshold for each.
2) Is BrightBridge interested in marketplace procurement (cloud marketplace procurement, reseller)?
3) Who is the economic buyer / budget owner (name & title)?
4) Who is the legal/finance reviewer and final signatory?

Suggested immediate next steps:
- Elena: confirm (1)-(4) above and share any procurement intake or PO template you require (we can pre-fill).
- Monica + Aditya: prepare a short mutual action plan and estimate for a 90-day pilot (deliver by EOD Wed).
- Marissa: standby for any approval questions and to coordinate procurement contacts if we need contract tweaks.

If you prefer, we can run the pilot via a Redwood-hosted contract and accept a PO, or we can route via a marketplace listing if that makes procurement easier for you. Either way, I want to map the signatory flow so there's no surprises.

Attachments: none yet — I will attach a short procurement checklist on the MAP we send.

Monica — thanks for the clear recap and the demo yesterday. Quick answers below, plus I'm attaching our procurement intake spreadsheet so your team can pre-fill.

1) Payment method: For enterprise purchases we prefer a PO routed through Ariba for anything above $50k ARR. For smaller engagements (sub-$5k monthly) we usually allow corporate card. There is a mid-band ($5k–$50k) that requires finance approval and sometimes a payment run via AP (which can add 10 business days).

2) Marketplace: We do use cloud marketplaces selectively. For pilot workloads where we want consolidated billing across cloud providers we prefer to purchase via our internal marketplace — but that requires the vendor to be listed. If Redwood can provide a marketplace SKU quickly, procurement can consider that route.

3) Economic buyer / budget owner: Victor Chen, VP Finance (v.chen@brightbridge.ai). He approved the pilot budget in principle on our call; he will own the PO.

4) Legal / Signatory: Legal will do a standard review — our procurement team sends everything to Legal. Final signatory is usually the CFO (Nisha Patel), but she delegates for pilots under $100k.

Timeline: If we go PO route, typical cycle is 2–3 weeks once Victor signs off and procurement has the contract. If we go card it can be done in 1–3 business days.

I've attached: BrightBridge_Procurement_Form.xlsx (fill this out and return).

Cheers,

--
Elena Morales

Good question. For marketplace listings we default to the marketplace provider T&Cs (no separate reseller agreement) for pilot SKUs. For enterprise contracts (annual committed spend) we typically do a vendor contract + standard PO.

To confirm signatory/budget flow for this pilot:
- Economic buyer / budget owner: Victor Chen (VP Finance) — will approve the PO.
- Procurement intake: procurement@brightbridge.ai — they asked that you pre-fill BrightBridge_Procurement_Form.xlsx (attached).
- Legal review: standard review (~3–5 business days).
- Final signatory: CFO Nisha Patel for >$100k, delegated approval possible for pilots under that threshold.

Next steps we propose:
1) Monica / Aditya: return the filled procurement form and a short mutual action plan (timeline + pilot acceptance criteria).
2) Victor / procurement: confirm internal PO timeline once they have the packet.
3) Redwood legal: share a one-page SOW and standard terms (we'll flag any redlines).

I've attached BrightBridge_PO_Policy.pdf that outlines internal PO rules — should help you map approvals.

Looking forward — if you want, Victor is available for a 15-min alignment call this week to unblock PO signoff.
